title: Battery Circularity Report 2025 (European Battery Circularity Association)
text:
Key figures
The European lithium-ion battery recycling value chain was worth EUR 3.4 billion in 2025, compared with EUR 2.9 billion in 2024, an increase of 18%. We expect EUR 4.0 billion in 2026.

Scope
Europe here means the EU-27, the EFTA countries (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland) and the United Kingdom. All lithium-ion feedstock is included: end-of-life EV packs, production scrap from cell and pack plants, and portable batteries. Value is service revenue plus the market value of recovered nickel, cobalt, lithium, manganese and copper at average 2025 prices. EV-related feedstock accounted for about 70% of tonnage.

Method
Figures come from a survey of the association's 41 member sites and public data for non-members. Because recovered materials are valued at market prices, the total moves with metal prices: lower lithium prices held back 2025 growth despite 26% more tonnes processed.

Outlook
Capacity is no longer the bottleneck for pre-treatment; refining capacity and feedstock supply are. Members call for faster permits for hydrometallurgical plants and for keeping black mass inside Europe.
